title: Adapting Pairs Trading to Gambling Markets A Case Study of the U.S. Presidential Election
abstract: arXiv:2609.22639v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pairs trading exploits mean reversion in the relationship between related assets. We adapt this idea to political betting markets by modelling the combined implied probability of the two major-party nominees with a latent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process whose mean-reversion level varies over time and whose observations contain additive noise. Model parameters are estimated from regularly sampled odds data using a state-space likelihood, with consecutive repeated values represented by a single retained observation and the elapsed number of sampling intervals preserved in the continuous-time transition. Parametric-bootstrap upper prediction bounds identify signal times at which the combined implied probability is likely to decline, and a no-intercept Bradley-Terry-type model selects the candidate-specific odds quote. The candidate-selection model is trained on 2020 U.S. presidential-election data and evaluated out of sample on 2024 data. The

translated_title: 将配对交易应用于博彩市场：以美国总统大选为例的案例研究
translated_abstract: 配对交易利用相关资产之间关系的均值回归特性。我们将这一思想应用于政治博彩市场，通过一个潜在Ornstein-Uhlenbeck过程来建模两大党总统候选人组合隐含概率，该过程的均值回归水平随时间变化，且观测值包含加性噪声。模型参数通过状态空间似然函数从定期采样的赔率数据中进行估计，其中连续重复的数值由单个保留观测值表示，并在连续时间转移中保留经过的采样区间数。参数化自助法（parametric bootstrap）的上预测界用于识别组合隐含概率可能下降的信号时点，而无截距的Bradley-Terry型模型用于选择特定候选人的赔率报价。候选人选择模型在2020年美国总统大选数据上进行训练，并在2024年数据上进行样本外评估。
tldr: 该论文将配对交易的均值回归思想引入政治博彩市场，用时变均值回归水平的Ornstein-Uhlenbeck过程建模两大党候选人组合隐含概率，结合参数化自助法预测上界与无截距Bradley-Terry型候选人选择模型，在2020年大选数据上训练并于2024年大选数据上完成样本外验证。
en_tdlr: This paper adapts pairs trading's mean-reversion concept to political betting markets by modeling the combined implied probability of two major-party nominees with a time-varying Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, combining parametric-bootstrap upper prediction bounds with an intercept-free Bradley-Terry-type candidate-selection model, trained on 2020 U.S. presidential election data and validated out-of-sample on 2024 data.
